# Review (pass 1, units only) — secret-history-087-092

Method: every `t` checked by script against the packet (447 words, every word once, in order, no unit crossing a §; `words` count = word count per unit; `p: true` on exactly the first unit of §§87–92, no extras: all correct, nothing to change). Then every note, `l`, `i` and morph read against the form, the Ming gloss in the packet and the published parts (01-06, 080-086 and the glossary-style morph glosses of all published parts). gloss.json not touched. units.json edited in place by script; the original is kept outside the repo.

## Findings refused (checked, left as is)

- Unit 13 note ("büleġe ... turns the whole into a habit") and unit 17 ("past of habit"), l "used-to-be": the published parts' morph glosses give -leġe as "past narrative: was, used to be", and 080-086 renders it variously; the Ming 有來 is a bare past. Left for consistency with the published glosses; the habit reading is stated only in the note and is mild.
- Unit 27 i "being driven off" (hüldežü, active "driving" in l): the note says the driver is unnamed and the geldings are the object; the English passive is a fair smoothing. Left.
- Unit 57 note "said ... to himself" against i "I said": harmless; the note and i do not conflict in sense.
- Unit 25 manaγar "next morning" vs unit 27 "this morning": both fit their contexts and the Ming 淸 / 淸早; the morph already records the difference.
- Unit 56 qubijalduja: -jaldu- given as one reciprocal; the note already marks the split uncertain. Left.
- Unit 59 "Önžē-ü" glossed with a genitive: the note flags it uncertain; no better analysis available from the Ming.
- Unit 40/41 cut after "bai;" inside the speech: legitimate sense-unit cut at Shiratori's punctuation; bi. is explained in the note.
- Unit 2 note "here 'your own' because it follows the imperative": odd phrasing, sense correct (reflexive refers to the addressee). Left.
- Remembered English: no other i matched a phrasing I could identify as a recalled translation; this cannot be verified without opening translations, which the conventions forbid.
- Word coverage, t exactness, p:true: no findings.
